business-narrative.name: Business Narrative
business-narrative.summary: Tell a business strategy or solution as a story: setting, challenge, tension, hero, plan, outcome. Useful for internal alignment decks, town halls, and any audience that responds better to story shape than to bullet lists.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Engage the audience and set expectations for the next twenty minutes. Tell them you're going to tell them a story — and then start telling it. Avoid a separate agenda slide; the introduction is the first scene.

beats.name: Setting
beats.description: Establish the world the story takes place in: the team, the market, the moment. Just enough context that the challenge will feel meaningful when it arrives.

beats.name: Challenge
beats.description: Identify the issue at hand. Concrete, specific, attributable. The challenge is the inciting incident — the thing that pulled the rest of the story into motion.

beats.name: Tension
beats.description: Raise the stakes. What happens if the challenge isn't met? Quantify the cost, name the people affected, surface the trade-offs that make the choice hard. Tension is what makes the audience lean in.

beats.name: Solution
beats.description: Reveal the strategy or hero of the story. Lead with what changes for the audience or customer when the solution is in place. This is the turn from problem to promise.

beats.name: Implementation
beats.description: Describe the path to success. Phases, owners, milestones, key bets. Show the audience that the solution has weight behind it — not just intent.

beats.name: Recap
beats.description: Bring the audience back to the surface with a clear summary of what was said and decided. Echo the language from the opening so the story feels closed.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Reinforce the key message and the call to action. End on the line you most want repeated in tomorrow's hallway conversations.
beats.instructions: Reinforce takeaways and call to action

candidates.name: Candidates
candidates.summary: Potential hires evaluating company, role, and people.
candidates.description: Candidates are weighing a major life decision and have many alternatives. Lead with mission and why-now, show the team they'll work with, and be honest about the stage. Avoid generic recruiting copy — specifics build trust faster than polish.

plan.name: Plan
plan.summary: Establish a roadmap, operating plan, or sequence of actions with owners and next steps.
plan.description: Use when the deck should turn strategy into coordinated action. Make sequencing, ownership, dependencies, risks, and checkpoints visible.
plan.outcome: The audience understands the plan and accepts the next actions.

conversational.name: Conversational
conversational.summary: Direct, dialog-style voice for podcasts, fireside chats, and small-group reviews.
conversational.description: Sound like one half of a real conversation. Ask questions on the slide and answer them; keep paragraphs short; lean into examples over abstractions. Useful when the deck is meant to support a discussion rather than to lecture.
voiceCues: Ask a question on the slide, then answer it on the next.
Use second person — speak to the room, not at it.
Lean on stories and concrete examples over abstract framing.
Keep each idea to one short paragraph; let the dialog do the rest.
avoid: Stuffing slides — leave room for the discussion.
Inside-baseball references the room may not share.
samplePhrases: Why now? Two things changed in the last six months.
Here's the part that surprised us — and what we did about it.
If you take one thing from this section, take this.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.description: A clean, minimalistic theme with a focus on simplicity and readability. Ideal for professional, straightforward presentations.

luxury.name: Luxury
luxury.summary: Muted metallic and deep tones for premium, high-stakes decks.
luxury.description: A restrained luxury palette with gold, terracotta, dark green, and blue-gray support for premium narratives.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

segoe-ui-light.name: Segoe UI Light
segoe-ui-light.description: Segoe UI Light is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Segoe UI Semilight for headings with Segoe UI Light for body text.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
